title: tenant-aware safeguarded traffic duplex and cost fencing
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: We need a production-safe way to run 'duplexed' traffic (primary + passive fork) for model rollouts and offline evaluation without blowing tenant budgets or exposing noisy tenants to performance regressions. Existing ad-hoc probes and large-scale forks have caused cost spikes and noisy metrics in the past.

Goal: Implement a tenancy-aware traffic-duplex pipeline that provides: (1) deterministic, budget-conscious sampling per-tenant; (2) workload isolation so forks cannot overload serving pools or interfere with latency SLOs; (3) chargeback instrumentation and automatic billing caps; (4) configurable rollback triggers and automated drain for mirrored variants. The pipeline must integrate with rollouts (canary/A-B) and Redwood's routing layer and expose observability hooks for quality/eval teams.

High-level design: incoming request flows through the gateway and enters the duplex controller which computes a per-tenant sampling decision using: tenant policy (budget share), historical traffic profile, and global safety gates. If selected, a non-blocking passive copy is forked into a mirrored queue on a separate tenancy-aware corridor; samples are annotated with a lightweight trace id and tenant hash. Mirrored requests are processed on dedicated worker pools (isolated instance groups) with quota tokens that expire hourly. Cost accrual uses a separate accounting pipeline that emits token-usage events to billing and cost dashboards. Automatic rollback will trigger when mirrored quality deltas or error-rate thresholds cross configured tolerances for a sustained window; in that case the controller will scale down mirroring for impacted tenants and create a canary incident for review.

Sampling algorithm: hybrid of reservoir per-tenant (to guarantee minimum sample) plus weighted-probabilistic sampling based on request rate and remaining budget. This prevents small tenants from being starved while bounding cost for very high-volume tenants. Sampling parameters are configurable per-tenant and inheritable from org defaults.

Isolation controls: mirrored traffic runs on separate autoscaling pools tagged by tenant bucket. Pools enforce soft concurrency caps and CPU/GPU quotas. Mirrored pools are rate-limited by a token-bucket that is refilled according to tenant commitments (Reserved capacity consumes tokens at a lower rate). Mirrored pools have lower scheduling priority and no external-facing SLA.

Cost controls and accounting: cost events are emitted in near-real-time to the console cost breakdown; per-request cost attribution includes model variant, sequence length bucket, and sampling multiplier to allow accurate chargebacks. A per-tenant spend guard will automatically pause mirroring when forecasted spend exceeds configured thresholds and notify the tenant owner.

Rollback and safety heuristics: automated triggers combine correctness regressions (n-gram divergence / hallucination metrics), latency regressions, and infrastructure errors. Triggers require a 3-tier confirmation (fast signal + confirmatory sample + sustained window) before automated rollback to avoid flapping. Rollback action includes: stop new mirror forks for impacted tenant, accelerate draining of existing mirrored work, and post a rollback annotation to the rollout timeline.

Non-goals: this ticket does not implement model-side instrumentation for hallucination scoring (that is a follow-up). It also does not include GUI features for tenant self-serve configuration (console work tracked separately).
implementation_notes:
Planned work items:
- Duplex controller: implement policy engine and per-tenant reservoir sampler (ENG task).
- Mirrored queue & corridor: durable queues with tenant isolation tags.
- Dedicated mirrored pools: k8s node pools with autoscaler knobs and quota enforcement.
- Cost emission: event schema + console integration (cost tag enrichment).
- Rollback orchestration: signal aggregator + drain API + rollout annotation.
- Tests: e2e smoke on staging, synthetic high-volume test, cost budget fuzz tests.

Approx timeline: 2-week spike -> 4-week MVP -> 2-week hardened rollout. Work will be split across runtime and gateway squads. See attached RFC for design trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant sampling honoring configured budgets with <5% deviation in first 1M requests
Mirrored processing executes on isolated pools without increasing primary tail latency by >5% under representative load
Cost events surface in console with per-tenant attribution and spend guard triggers at configured thresholds
Automated rollback triggers correctly stop mirroring and post rollout annotations in 95% of injected fault scenarios in staging
risk_and_mitigation:
Risks: cost overruns from misconfigured sampling, noisy metrics causing false rollbacks, and tenant cross-impact from improperly isolated pools. Mitigations: conservative default sampling, multi-signal rollback confirmation, hard token-based budget caps, and safety flag to disable mirroring globally. Will add circuit-breaker and emergency kill switch accessible to SRE.

Operational notes: enable detailed tracing for first 48h of any tenant onboarding to duplexed traffic and run cost forecast job daily for early warning.
comments: 2026-02-19: Spike complete. Baseline reservoir+prob sampler implementation shows predictable sample distribution in local sim (skew handled).

2026-02-25: Design review with PM and runtime team. PM requested explicit spend-guard notification flow; runtime asked for a separate mirrored pool discovery API. Action: add cost-emission schema and pool-tagging contract. Link to RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/duplex-rfc

2026-03-02: Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/9123. Early staging run revealed increased CPU pressure on mirrored pools due to synchronous pre-processing; fixed by making mirror path fully async and adding backpressure. PR awaiting perf sign-off.

2026-03-10: QA noted flaky rollback confirm step when signals are noisy; adjusted confirmation logic to require a confirmatory sample plus 3-minute sustained window. Added integration test to simulate flapping error rates.
2026-03-13: Security review scheduled for 2026-03-18. Need to validate that mirrored payloads respect PII redaction and KMS tagging for Private customers. Assigned to security review board.
2026-03-14: Beta rollout plan drafted: start with internal tenants + 5 pilot customers. Console feature ticket created for tenant opt-in UI (PM-4593).
